newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati suit delayed on technicality.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati suit delayed on technicality.

text.p: A case brought by ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri against the East Jakarta mayor was postponed for two weeks on Tuesday after government lawyers failed to sign court documents they had lodged.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, sued Mayor Sudarsono after he closed down a temporary office she had opened on the grounds that it contravened residential zoning regulations.
The suit alleges the mayor did not have the authority to close the office in September.

Megawati opened the office after her supporters were evicted from the headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party on July 27 in a move that sparked the worst riots in Jakarta in more than 20 years. Megawati was ousted as party chairman in June by a government-backed faction.

Max Lamuda, a lawyer from Megawati's legal team, said Judge Soemaryono of the Jakarta State Administrative Court adjourned the case until November 19 during the closed hearing that lasted less than five minutes.

"The letter of authority was only signed by the East Jakarta mayor. It was not complete as the (government) lawyers had not signed it. I suggested they just sign it now, but the judge said they should do it later," Lamuda told Reuters at the court.
"The judge said the letter of authority was like a contract and both parties had to sign it."
